Alex / Marissa — reviewed. I prefer a short, explicit clause in the order form to avoid separate addenda. My redline suggestions are attached (legal_redline_acme_v1.docx) and an extract below for quick copy/paste:

"Termination for Convenience (Pilot Exception). Notwithstanding Section X (Term and Termination), for the initial term only, Customer may elect to terminate this Order Form upon providing thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Provider. If Customer exercises this right, Customer will pay a termination fee equal to one (1) month of committed subscription fees, pro-rated to the effective date of termination. This one-time right shall automatically expire at the end of the initial twelve (12) month term and shall not apply to subsequent renewal terms.

Mutual Notice Alternative. If Customer prefers mutual notice in lieu of the pilot exception, replace the notice period in Section X with: both parties shall provide no less than ninety (90) days' prior written notice to terminate at the end of any then-current term.
"

Rationale: the one-time 30-day pilot exception limits our exposure (nominal fee) while meeting their governance requirement. The 90-day mutual notice option is allowable but increases churn risk on renewals.

Please confirm commercial tradeoffs. If Sales is comfortable with the 1-month fee, Legal can produce a short amendment for signature and we can include the clause directly in the order form.

Attachments: legal_redline_acme_v1.docx, term_clause_snippet.txt
